text:
sophia: Quick follow-up from the RFC: we need to settle the onboarding handshake boundaries before we land the bench slice changes. Main question — do we keep the existing Descriptor v1 surface for the intake gateway and add a thin v2 shim in the prober, or break compatibility and require vendors to emit v2 descriptors?
ria: I vote for the thin shim. minimizes churn for integrators. but it adds complexity in the gateway.
lee: +1 on shim. If we do shim we should add a clear contract: shim must be idempotent and stateless. Also we need telemetry to detect cases where shim diverges from canonical v2.
omar: If we accept shim, we need a compatibility test in the smokebench that asserts parity of outputs within epsilon across descriptors. Otherwise we will accumulate silent regressions.
sophia: Agreed. Proposal: add a nightly compat job that runs a fixed set of golden inputs and compares outputs with a tolerance table. If mismatch rate > 0.5% for any model, create a regression ticket.
alex: How expensive will that be? Running full bench nightly could be heavy. Can we run a lightweight sample plus periodic full runs?
lee: plan: lightweight daily sample (~100 golden prompts) and weekly full slice (~5k prompts) on a representative shard. Also cache embeddings/kv to speed runs.
ria: For the tolerance table: we need per-model and per-metric tolerances (logprob drift, tokenization deltas, latency variance). I'd prefer we store tolerances in the model manifest so onboards can opt-in to tighter checks.
omar: +1 manifest-level tolerances. also keep a fallback path: if a model chooses no tolerances we apply conservative defaults (eg 1e-3 logprob, 2 tokens delta).
ci-bot: ci: nightly-compat job queued for models: (redwood-open-1, llama-ish, quant-lite) — see CI run link http://ci/redwood/5524307890 
sophia: For interface boundaries: gateway should only normalize old->v2 shapes. heavy lifting (quant flags, bench hints) stays in the prober and bench runner. That keeps gateway fast.
lee: Agree. Also add an explicit header X-Onboard-Descriptor-Version so we can trace incidents where wrong descriptor used.
alex: One more: rollout strategy. We should gate v2-only on a canary channel for early-adopters. Plan: start canary for 2 weeks with shadow traffic + golden-slate checks, then 50% traffic staged.
sophia: Sounds good. I'll draft a small RFC addendum with: shim contract, nightly/weekly bench cadence, manifest tolerance schema, header, and canary rollout plan.
ria: small nit: include debug endpoint in the prober to replay a single golden input and attach model fingerprints. helped me debug last week.
sophia: added. I'll ping eng-infra for quota for weekly full runs.
omar: thx. can someone create the initial tolerance defaults PR? I can review.
lee: I can start it tomorrow.
sophia: awesome — closing loop: i'll post the addendum here once written and assign follow-ups. :thumbsup:
